title: Chapter 9 — Campaign Season
description: Tamara's mother and your sponsor are fighting for the same seat, and the campus is their battlefield.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Election season. Royal Crest wakes up covered in posters: Owó Ńlá in agbada, Hon. Mrs. Ronke in white. Someone has drawn moustaches on both. Equal opportunity.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: My mother is doing a youth town hall on campus on Friday. Your Honourable is doing a "rally" on Thursday. (She looks at you.) Everyone is going to watch which one you stand at.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: Thursday. Owó Ńlá scholars in the front row in green. ₦5,000 each and lunch. Those who don't come... will be noted.

options.text: Front row at Owó Ńlá's rally, in green.
Volunteer for Hon. Ronke's town hall. Openly.
The library. Both days. Let them fight.

beats.speaker: owoNla
beats.text: (on stage, pointing at the front row) These are MY scholars! The future! (He calls you up.) Young man, tell them: who is the father of Iyana-Wahala youth?

beats.speaker: owoNla
beats.text: A microphone. A thousand phones filming.

options.text: "Our mothers are, sir." Smile. Hand back the microphone.
Take the microphone and announce you are joining the Honourable's Youth Wing full time.

beats.speaker: owoNla
beats.text: (delighted, into the microphone) You see?! A scholar who understands loyalty! Barrister, give him a car. A small one. With my face on it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You drop out at the end of the semester. Nobody minds. The Youth Wing pays better than a degree, and you are very, very good at microphones.

beats.title: Youth Leader
beats.summary: You traded the degree for a microphone and a small car with somebody else's face on it.

perfect.toast: The hall stands up for the student who asked Ronke the hardest question. Ronke stands up too.

beats.speaker: ronke
beats.text: (after the town hall) You asked me about market toilets in front of my donors. (A pause.) Good. That's the only question I'm afraid of.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: (a text) The Honourable saw the town hall photos. The Foundation is reviewing "loyalty" this quarter.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two days in the library. Thursday you hear drums from the field. Friday you hear applause from the lecture theatre. You read the whole of Samuelson chapter nine.

beats.objective: Go back to the hostel. Through the back gate is shorter.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: (at the back gate, counting cash) Election season is Christmas for the Dons. Owó Ńlá's people pay us to scatter Ronke's town hall next week. You want in? Easy money.

variants.text: (at the back gate, counting cash) Member. Owó Ńlá is paying us to scatter Ronke's town hall next week. You're coming. That isn't a question.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: He holds out a red bandana.

options.text: Take it. One night of shouting.
Warn Tamara about the plan tonight.

beats.title: Campaign Season
beats.summary: Two candidates, one campus, and everybody watching where you stood.
